name: Washington Square

function.note: 'The open square immediately south of' the Ogden house (Andreas vol. 2, p. 759).

built.note: An open square before the fire (p. 759); when it was laid out is not researched here, and 1842 stands for it.

research_note: WASHINGTON SQUARE, built by T-3689 for the 1871 scene: the open square on the North Side between Clark and Dearborn Streets, south of Mahlon D. Ogden's house. 'Washington Square had been filled with fugitives earlier in the night, but they had been compelled to flee, leaving their household goods scattered on the ground. These light goods quickly vanished in the flames'; 'the open square immediately south of it' is one reason Andreas gives that the Ogden house was ordinarily beyond danger (Andreas vol. 2, p. 759). The square is laid on today's Washington Square Park, between Clark, Dearborn and Walton Streets; its fence is reconstructed.

documented_range.note: Open on the night of the fire (Andreas vol. 2, p. 759); the scene's phase begins in 1860.

position.symbolic_location: Between Clark and Dearborn Streets, south of the Ogden house's block (Oak Street, now Walton).
position.note: Inside the street lines of today's Washington Square Park (the City's centrelines of Clark, Dearborn and Walton Streets, data/context/1871/modern_clip.json, less half each street and its walk); its south line is taken a little north of Delaware Place's line. The footprint's origin is local E 571.0 N 1391.0.

derivation.reason: Laid inside the modern park's street lines; no 1871 survey of the square is in the repository.

footprint.note: The open ground of the square, inside its streets.
